question: Which statement best describes What tsconfig.json does?
options: esModuleInterop makes CommonJS and ES module imports interoperate cleanly, so import express from 'express' works even though express is a CommonJS module. It emits helper code and adjusts how default and namespace imports of CJS modules behave; it is on by default in modern setups and almost always wanted.

tsconfig.json marks a directory as the root of a TypeScript project and tells tsc (and editors/build tools) which files to compile and with what options. Running tsc in a folder with it uses these settings; tools like Vite, ts-node, and your IDE read the same file so behavior is consistent everywhere.

strict: true turns on a family of strict type-checking flags at once — including strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, strictFunctionTypes, strictBindCallApply, and more. It is the single most important setting for catching bugs: it forces you to handle null/undefined and to type values that would otherwise silently become any.

target sets the JavaScript language level the compiler emits (e.g. ES2022) — it controls downleveling of syntax like async/await and optional chaining. module sets the module system of the output (esnext, commonjs, nodenext). Together they decide what runtime your emitted JS is meant for.
